geography.note: Boundaries and direct/indirect/induced definitions chosen to match Berkeley's 2025 Creative Economy Economic Impact Analysis so results are comparable to a study the City already commissioned.

_meta.status: ILLUSTRATIVE DEFAULTS. Every value below is a modeled or stipulated placeholder pending the data-gap register in evidence_sources. None is a measured fact. The Kite Festival last ran 2017-2019; 2020-2022 were disrupted by COVID and are not valid no-festival controls.
_meta.citation_disclaimer: Do NOT use the Creative Economy report's portfolio-wide '$197 catalyzed per grant dollar' as an event multiplier. That figure describes a portfolio of organizations, not the marginal return of one event.

event_scenarios.label: 1. No festival
event_scenarios.note: Counterfactual baseline. Public resources put to their ordinary use.

event_scenarios.label: 2. Full festival, former model
event_scenarios.note: Reconstructs the ~2017-2019 operating model: free parking, no managed demand.

event_scenarios.label: 4. Full festival, managed access
event_scenarios.note: Paid/reserved parking, shuttle, bike valet, added AC Transit service, sponsorship requirements.

event_scenarios.label: 5. Alternative waterfront event
event_scenarios.note: Different event using the same public resources - the opportunity-cost comparator.

visitor_spending._units: Dollars per person per event-day, 2025$. attribution = 1 - would_visit_anyway blend (festival-attribution factor). retention = share of spending that lands inside Berkeley.

io_multipliers._note: Applied to incremental, Berkeley-retained direct spending. IMPLAN row is primary (matches Creative Economy study); RIMS II is an independent cross-check. Ranges express multiplier uncertainty, not a single incontrovertible figure.

city_service_costs._note: Marina Fund chart-of-accounts framing. Each line tagged so an accounting allocation is never mistaken for a true marginal cost. Values are per full 2-day event unless noted; one-day scenarios scale by event_days/2 for variable lines.

managed_access_addon.note: Shuttle, satellite parking, bike valet, added AC Transit service under scenario 4.

city_revenues._note: Modeled where transaction data cannot be released; observed where legally available. Sales-tax share is the City's local share of taxable Berkeley-retained incremental sales.
city_revenues.note_sponsorship: Sponsorship is carried on event_scenarios, not here, because it is an event-operations revenue, not a City tax.

parking_inventory._note: Berkeley Waterfront parking framework identified 2,000+ spaces but flagged limited utilization data. Treat capacity as modeled.

community_outcomes._note: Kept as visible indicators, not forced into dollars. Measured by a structured post-event survey. A later stated-preference study could estimate willingness-to-pay - deliberately excluded from this first release.

model_assumptions._displacement_note: Share of incremental local activity that is not truly new to Berkeley - deterred waterfront customers, crowded-out park users, purchases merely shifted to the festival weekend, other events that cannot occur. Subtracted before multipliers. This is the gross-to-net step.
model_assumptions.confidence_target: 80% interval reported on every headline result
